activity_context.topic_title: Phase Portraits for Decoupled Linear Systems

feedback.problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=6x(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=4y(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following could represent the phase portrait of the decoupled system above?
feedback.worked_solution:
Writing our system in matrix form, we have

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}6 & 0 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}]x(t)
$$

where $x(t)=[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}].$

Since our system is decoupled, its eigenvectors are the following:

- Eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}=6$ with the corresponding eigenvector $[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$

- Eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{2}=4$ with the corresponding eigenvector $[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

The general solution of the system is

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}{e}^{6t}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}{e}^{4t}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, notice that:

- The straight-line solutions of the form
${c}_{1}{e}^{6t}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$
lie on the $x$-axis. Since ${e}^{6t}\to \infty $ as $t\to \infty ,$ these solutions approach infinity as $t\to \infty .$

- The straight-line solutions of the form
${c}_{2}{e}^{4t}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$
lie on the $y$-axis. Since ${e}^{4t}\to \infty $ as $t\to \infty ,$ these solutions approach infinity as $t\to \infty .$

Among the given options, there are two phase portraits satisfying these conditions:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14069185/assets/2473117cdca4318187b94374820c0a12576e998e7f631a6e7bf51e56c985be43.png)

Let's consider the solutions $x(t)={c}_{1}{e}^{6t}$ and $y(t)={c}_{2}{e}^{4t}$ provided that ${c}_{1},{c}_{2}\ne 0.$ Then,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{{y}^{′}(t)}{{x}^{′}(t)}=\frac{({c}_{2}{e}^{4t})^{′}}{({c}_{1}{e}^{6t})^{′}}=\frac{4{c}_{2}{e}^{4t}}{6{c}_{1}{e}^{6t}}=\frac{2{c}_{2}}{3{c}_{1}}{e}^{-2t}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\to 0$ as $t\to \infty ,$ meaning that the tangents to the solution become more and more horizontal as we move away from the origin. This corresponds to the following phase portrait:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14069185/assets/e8110ea6d6a113e72e35502030afb495a23bc81106d64874582d03aae81b7c73.png)
